bandReport.notes: 20 questions, 4+6+4+6 across p10/p12/p14/p16 (printed pages 11/13/15/17). NO Directions/shared-context block anywhere in this band — every question is standalone, so no setLabel is used. Seam check: p08 (printed 9, band b1) ends with Q26 complete, all four options printed, and no Directions block open at its foot, so Q27 is a clean start. p18 (printed 19, band b3) opens with Q47 complete and standalone, and my Q46 ends complete at the foot of p16, so nothing straddles either seam and no question is unowned. Watermark crossings on this band: Q28, Q30, Q32, Q35(d), Q36, Q38, Q40, Q42(b)(c), Q43, Q45, Q46 — every one of those was re-cropped at 3.5-6x and read individually. questions.stem:
Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of the equation
\(x^2 - p(x + 1) - q = 0\)
What is
\(\frac{\alpha^2 + 2\alpha + 1}{\alpha^2 + 2\alpha + q} + \frac{\beta^2 + 2\beta + 1}{\beta^2 + 2\beta + q}\)
equal to?

If the sum of the roots of the equation
\(\frac{1}{2x + p} + \frac{1}{2x + q} = \frac{1}{r}\)
is zero, then what is \(r\) equal to?

Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be the roots of the equation \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) and \(p_n = \alpha^n + \beta^n\), where \(n > 1\). What is
\(ap_{n+1} + bp_n + cp_{n-1}\)
equal to?

If \(p\), \(q\) and \(r\) are in AP, then what is
\(p^3 + 3pr(p + r) + r^3\)
equal to?
If \(\frac{1}{b - a} + \frac{1}{b - c} = \frac{2}{b}\), then \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are in

options.label: D
options.text: Neither in AP nor in GP nor in HP

questions.stem: Let \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) and \(S\) be the sum of \(n\) terms, \(2n\) terms, \(3n\) terms and \(4n\) terms respectively of an AP such that \(Q = 3P\). Which one of the following is correct?
In a GP, the 3rd, 5th and 7th terms are \(x\), \(x^2 + 2\) and \(x^3 + 10\) respectively, where \(x > 1\). What is the 8th term?
If \((1 + i)^n - 16 = 0\), where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) and \(n\) is a positive integer, then what is the least value of \(n\)?
What is \(i \times i^4 \times i^9 \times i^{16} \times \ldots \times i^{576}\), where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\), equal to?

If \(z = x + iy\) be such that \(\left| \frac{z + \lambda i}{z - \lambda i} \right| = 1\), where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\) and \(\lambda\) is a positive real number, then which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. \(z\) lies on the line \(y = x\).
II. The amplitude of \(z\) is \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
Select the answer using the code given below.

What is
\(\begin{vmatrix} \frac{1}{a} & bc & a^3 \\ \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} & c(a + b) & a^3 + b^3 \\ \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} & ab + bc + ca & a^3 + b^3 + c^3 \end{vmatrix}\)
equal to?

If
\(ae + bg = cf + dh = p\), \(af + bh = ce + dg = q\)
then what is
\(\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} \times \begin{vmatrix} e & f \\ g & h \end{vmatrix}\)
equal to?

If
\(x + ay + a^2 z = 1\), \(x + by + b^2 z = 1\), \(x + cy + c^2 z = 1\)
where \(a \ne b \ne c\), then what is \(x + y + z\) equal to?

questions.stem:
Let
\(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -\tan\theta \\ \tan\theta & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \tan\theta \\ -\tan\theta & 1 \end{pmatrix}\)
If \(C = AB^{-1}\), then what is \(\det(C)\) equal to?

What is the coefficient of \(x^{2n}\) in the expansion of the following?
\((1 + x)^{2n} \left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)^{2n}\)

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements in respect of the expansion of \((x^2 + x^{-2} + 2)^4\) :
I. The number of terms in the expansion is 5.
II. One of the coefficients in the expansion has a maximum value equal to 70.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

questions.stem: If \(x^2 - 2x\cos\theta + 1 = 0\), then what is the magnitude of \(x\)?
flags: Printed as-is: option (a) offers \(-1\) as a candidate MAGNITUDE, which cannot be negative. Re-cropped at 6x on p16 and the minus sign is sharp and upright, so this is what the booklet prints, not a scan artefact. Not repaired.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements in respect of sets \(A\) and \(B\) :
I. If \(x \in A\) and \(A \in B\), then \(x \in B\).
II. If \(A \subset B\) and \(x \notin B\), then \(x \notin A\).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.subtopic: Set Operations, Identities, and Cartesian Products of Sets
flags: Forced subtopic fit. This question is about membership vs subset logic (\(\in\) against \(\subset\)), not about set operations, identities or Cartesian products. The other two Sets & Relations subtopics are worse — it involves no counting and no relation. Closest available name chosen per the brief.
